experiments.scope: Reduced-width program check at claim-shaped budgets: width 12 bits, fresh budget 80, total 272, on F restricted to a per-trial keyed coset of 2^12 inputs and truncated to its first 12 digest bits. Tests the restricted, truncated function only; the step to 256 bits is the extrapolation stated in proof.md Section 8.
experiments.hypothesis: Program check at width 12: the Section 3 algorithm with fresh budget M=80 (M^2/2^13=0.7812 against 0.7684 in the claim, the rounding of M up to an integer), theta=2^-2, L_max=64, total budget 272, run on the three-round digest of 0^32 || (R | v) for a per-trial offset R = SHA-256(seed || 'coset') with its low 12 bits cleared, truncated to its first 12 bits, returns a host-verified 12-bit-prefix collision in a fraction of trials not below 0.75 times that of a uniformly random 12-bit function (the H1 boundary at this width). Reference measured by the author over 10,000 trials with a fresh random function per trial: q=0.4581 (99% CI [0.4453, 0.4710]). The same program on the keyed F over 10,000 trials with the author's seed labels: 0.4574 (99% CI [0.4446, 0.4703]), ratio 0.999. Predicted successes in 256 trials at ratio 1: 117.3. Floor at the H1 boundary: 69, the 0.5% quantile of Binomial(256, 0.75 q). A count below 69 would mean the search on F at this width succeeds less than three quarters as often as on a random function and would send the author back to the program and to F at this width; a count at or above 69 says that the program runs under the executor and finds host-verifiable pairs at a rate not below the H1 boundary at this width. Neither outcome is evidence about width 256, and no claimed number depends on this count. The author's own 256-seed run in the organizer's request format returned 121; the organizer's seeds differ (standard deviation about 8). Only the returned pairs are host-verified; observations are participant counters. See proof.md Section 8.

experiments.scope: Unbudgeted run at width 16 (hard stop 2^20 steps) on a per-trial keyed coset of 2^16 inputs: checks that the shipped search finds a host-verifiable 16-bit-prefix collision of the three-round digest in every trial, and reports step counts (untrusted) for comparison with the birthday prediction.
experiments.hypothesis: Every trial returns a pair of distinct 64-byte messages of the family 0^32 || x whose three-round digests agree on the first 16 bits (256 of 256 expected; any trial returning no pair would indicate a defect in the search or a function on which the walk cannot find a collision within 2^20 steps). Author's run: 256 of 256, mean 335.8 total steps against a random-function prediction of about 340, median 320, max 841. Observations are participant counters and are not host-verified. See proof.md Section 8.
